title: Factors for Continuation of Government's Cost-of-living Support
what_it_is: Factors for Continuation of Government's Cost-of-living Support

sections.label: Cost-of-living support factors
sections.summary: Government says it monitors economic conditions and adjusts cost-of-living support, having provided Budget 2025 support and structural social support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance in relation to the Government’s statement in May 2025 that the Government will provide cost-of-living support for as long as it is needed, what are the factors that determine whether such Government support should continue, given that inflation has moderated, but cost of living anxieties remain elevated.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: We recognise that whilst inflation has moderated, Singaporeans are still adjusting to higher price levels.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: And that is why we provided additional support for Singaporeans in Budget 2025, including Community Development Council (CDC) vouchers and additional U-Save rebates.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Beyond transitional cost-of-living support, we have also strengthened structural social support in housing, healthcare, education and retirement to provide Singaporeans with assurance at every stage of life.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: We will continue to monitor economic conditions closely and adjust cost-of-living support as necessary.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: In the longer term, the best way to help Singaporeans is to have broad-based and inclusive real wage growth.

sections.label: Data and anxiety basis
sections.summary: Minister says support depends on whether data bears out sentiment and anxiety, and anxiety without real basis may not need additional support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The short answer to that is, we have to start, first, with data and if sentiment and anxiety are borne out by the data and there is a real need, then, of course, we will step in to do more.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But if we have a situation where there is anxiety, which is without real basis – and we can understand how that happens, sometimes, where people get concerned because others are talking about it; and then others talk about it, then, you have a general anxiety, but there is no real basis for that anxiety – then, there may not be a need to provide additional support for that.

sections.label: Targeted support and behaviour
sections.summary: Minister says circumstances determine support, and targeted subsets are based on need or to drive behaviour like SkillsFuture credits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, depending on what the circumstances are, we will see.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And then, for targeted subsets, again, the general principle is that we look to need or, sometimes, when we are trying to drive a certain form of behaviour, like when we wanted to encourage people with lifelong learning, we introduced the SkillsFuture credits.
